lessons.title: Getting ready to plant tea
lessons.html:
Before planting

Tea bushes can live and produce leaf for many years. Planting them well is the start of a good tea field. Young tea plants are grown in the nursery in sleeves (plastic bags). When they are big enough, they are planted out in the field.

What the field needs

Your supervisor will tell you which field to plant. The field is usually prepared before you start:

  • The land is cleared and the soil is loosened.
  • Contour lines or terraces may be made on slopes so rain does not wash the soil away.
  • Lines are marked with pegs and string to show where the rows go.

Tools and materials

  • Hoe, spade or pick to make planting holes
  • A measuring stick to space the holes
  • The young tea plants in sleeves
  • A knife or blade to cut the sleeve
  • Fertiliser or compost, if your supervisor says
  • Water, if the soil is dry
  • Mulch, such as grass

Taking plants from the nursery

  1. Water the plants in the nursery before you take them out. Wet soil in the sleeve holds together.
  2. Choose healthy plants: green leaves, strong stem, no pests.
  3. Carry plants upright in crates or trays. Do not carry them by the stem.
  4. Keep them in the shade in the field. Plant them the same day.

Safety

  • Wear boots and gloves. Use a hat and sunscreen.
  • Keep tools sharp but carry them with the blade down.
  • Keep a safe distance from other workers when you swing a hoe or pick.
  • Watch for snakes in long grass. Never try to catch or kill a snake; move away and tell your supervisor.
  • Drink water often.

lessons.title: Planting the bush and finishing the job
lessons.html:
Making the hole

  1. Find the peg or mark where the plant goes. Keep to the spacing the supervisor gives you.
  2. Dig a hole deeper and wider than the sleeve. Put the topsoil on one side and the subsoil on the other side.
  3. Loosen the bottom of the hole.
  4. Mix in compost or fertiliser only if your supervisor tells you, and only the amount given.

Planting

  1. Cut the bottom of the sleeve off. Then cut the side of the sleeve from bottom to top.
  2. Lower the plant into the hole. Gently pull the sleeve away. Do not break the soil around the roots.
  3. The top of the soil from the sleeve should be level with the top of the field soil. Do not plant too deep or too high.
  4. Fill the hole with topsoil first, around the roots, then subsoil.
  5. Press the soil firmly with your hands or foot around the plant, not on it. There should be no air holes.
  6. Make a small dip around the plant so water collects.
  7. Water the plant if the soil is dry.
  8. Put mulch around the plant, but not touching the stem.

Take all the plastic sleeves out of the field. Plastic left in the soil does not rot and pollutes the land.

Finishing the job

  • Count the plants you planted and tell your supervisor. Write it down if you were asked to.
  • Put back any plants you did not plant in the shade and water them.
  • Collect the empty sleeves, pegs and string.
  • Clean the tools and put them away.

In the weeks after planting, young plants need water if it does not rain, weeding, and checking for pests. Dead plants are replaced (gap filling).

Key points

  • Water nursery plants before taking them out and keep them in shade.
  • Dig the hole bigger than the sleeve and keep topsoil apart.
  • Remove the sleeve without breaking the root ball.
  • Plant at the same level, press firm and water.
  • Pick up all plastic and count the plants.

options.text: Wet soil in the sleeve holds together around the roots
So you do not need to water in the field
